questions.question_text: Staffing is the managerial function that deals with:
options: Guiding and motivating the people to put in their best efforts
Setting the objectives and the plans for the units of the firm
Filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure
Comparing the actual results against the standards that were set

questions.question_text: Which of these is the correct sequence of the staffing process?
options: Manpower planning, recruitment, selection, placement, training
Selection, recruitment, manpower planning, placement, appraisal
Placement, selection, recruitment, appraisal, manpower planning
Recruitment, manpower planning, training, selection, placement

questions.question_text: Human resource planning means:
options: Forecasting the demand for and supply of employees to meet future needs
Training the existing employees in the use of the new technology
Fixing the salary scales for the various jobs in the organisation
Selecting the candidates who are best suited for the current vacancies
questions.explanation: Right number, right kind, right time.

questions.question_text: The process of searching for prospective employees and encouraging them to apply is:
options: Selection
Recruitment
Induction
Placement

questions.question_text: Choosing the best candidates from among the applicants is:
options: Recruitment
Promotion
Selection
Orientation

questions.question_text: Recruitment is called a positive process while selection is a negative process because:
options: Recruitment attracts many candidates while selection rejects the unsuitable ones
Both of them reject the candidates who do not have the right qualifications
Recruitment rejects candidates while selection attracts many applicants
Both of them attract the candidates who are available in the market

questions.question_text: Filling a vacancy by promoting an existing employee is an example of:
options: Internal source of recruitment
Indirect recruitment through media
External source of recruitment
Direct recruitment through campus

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an external source of recruitment?
options: Promotion of a junior
Campus recruitment
Transfer from another department
Recall of former employees on leave

questions.question_text: An advantage of internal recruitment is that it:
options: Motivates the existing employees and reduces the cost of hiring
Brings in new ideas and experience from outside the firm
Avoids any dissatisfaction among employees who are not promoted
Gives a larger pool of candidates to choose from

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of external recruitment is that it:
options: Limits the choice to a few candidates in the firm
Leads to stagnation in the organisation
Prevents the entry of fresh talent into the firm
Is costly and may demotivate the existing employees

questions.question_text: Recruitment through advertisements in newspapers is an example of:
options: Transfer
Internal recruitment
External recruitment
Employee referral

questions.question_text: Placing the employee on the job for which he or she is selected is:
options: Placement
Training
Promotion
Induction

questions.question_text: Induction or orientation helps the new employee to:
options: Learn the technical skills required for the promotion
Get transferred to a department of his own choice
Become familiar with the organisation and its rules
Get a higher salary in the first year of service

questions.question_text: The correct order of the steps in the selection process is:
options: Job offer, test, interview, screening, medical exam, reference check
Reference check, interview, test, job offer, medical exam, screening
Preliminary screening, selection test, interview, reference check, medical exam, job offer
Interview, preliminary screening, medical exam, job offer, reference check, test

questions.question_text: Which of these tests measures the ability of a candidate to learn a skill in the future?
options: Personality test
Intelligence test
Achievement test
Aptitude test

questions.question_text: A test of the candidate's existing knowledge and skills is an:
options: Achievement or proficiency test of current competence
Personality test of the traits and the temperament
Aptitude test of the capacity to learn in future
Interest test of the preferences for the type of work

questions.question_text: Training is defined as a process aimed at:
options: Fixing the salary of the employees for their jobs
Preparing the employees for higher positions in the future
Choosing the best employees for the senior positions
Improving the knowledge and skills of the employees for the present job

questions.question_text: Development is a process that focuses on:
options: The orientation of the new employees to the working conditions
The immediate skill needs of the employee in the present job
The termination of the employee in cases of poor performance
The long-term growth of the employee to take on future responsibilities

questions.question_text: The difference between training and development is that training is:
options: For managers only while development is for the workers only
For the workers only while development is for the managers only
Career-oriented and long-term while development is job-oriented and short-term
Job-oriented and short-term while development is career-oriented and long-term

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an on-the-job training method?
options: Lectures
Job rotation
Case studies
Simulation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an off-the-job training method?
options: Job rotation across departments
Apprenticeship under a skilled worker
Classroom lectures
Coaching by a superior

questions.question_text: Vestibule training is a method in which:
options: Employees learn by moving from one job to another job in the firm
Employees are trained in a simulated work environment away from the actual shop floor
Employees learn by watching a skilled worker at the actual workplace
Employees learn through the case studies in a classroom

questions.question_text: Apprenticeship training combines:
options: Only the classroom learning of the theory
Only the simulation of the work environment
Only the reading of books and manuals
On-the-job experience with the theoretical learning

questions.question_text: In the "case study" method of training:
options: Trainees move across various departments of the firm
Trainees analyse real or imaginary situations and suggest solutions
Trainees are given lectures by the experts
Trainees work with the actual machines under supervision

questions.question_text: Role playing as a training method is useful for developing:
options: Technical skills in using machines
Physical skills required on the shop floor
Knowledge of company rules and policies
Interpersonal and communication skills

questions.question_text: Performance appraisal is the process of:
options: Selecting the candidates who are applying for a job in the firm
Training the employees in the new methods of production
Deciding the pay scales for the various posts in the firm
Evaluating the performance of employees against the set standards

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of performance appraisal?
options: Deciding on the promotions and transfers of employees
Giving feedback on the work to the employees
Selecting candidates for vacancies from outside the firm
Identifying the training needs of the employees

questions.question_text: The "halo effect" in performance appraisal is when:
options: A rater is harsh on all the employees without exception
A rater lets one outstanding trait influence the rating on all the other traits
A rater is influenced by the most recent performance of the employee
A rater rates all employees as average to avoid conflicts with them

questions.question_text: The "central tendency" error in appraisal occurs when the rater:
options: Rates all employees very low
Rates all employees very high
Rates all employees near the average
Rates only the recent performance

questions.question_text: A 360-degree appraisal involves feedback from:
options: The employee being appraised, through self-rating alone
Superiors, peers, subordinates and sometimes customers
The HR department of the firm, through the records alone
The immediate superior of the employee alone

questions.question_text: Management by Objectives as an appraisal method evaluates employees on the basis of:
options: Their seniority and length of service in the firm
Achievement of the jointly agreed targets
Their personality traits as seen by the superior
Their attendance and punctuality in the firm

questions.question_text: The "graphic rating scale" appraises employees by:
options: Describing the critical incidents in the essay form
Checking the employees against the standard time
Rating the traits on a scale from poor to excellent
Comparing the employees against each other in a ranking

questions.question_text: Ranking employees from best to worst is the:
options: Ranking method
Management by objectives method
Critical incident method
Graphic scale method

questions.question_text: Compensation to employees includes:
options: Only the basic salary that is paid every month
Wages, salaries, bonuses and benefits
Only the share in the profits paid out every year
Only the bonus that is paid on the festival days

questions.question_text: Job evaluation is a process of:
options: Estimating the cost of the training given on the job
Determining the relative worth of jobs in the organisation
Evaluating the performance of the employee on the job
Judging the qualifications of the candidates for the job

questions.question_text: Which of these methods of job evaluation is the simplest?
options: Ranking method
Classification method
Point method
Factor comparison method

questions.question_text: A pay structure based on equal pay for equal work is dependent upon:
options: Recruitment
Induction
Performance appraisal
Job evaluation

questions.question_text: A wage incentive paid for exceeding the production target is an example of:
options: Fringe benefit
Non-financial incentive
Financial incentive
Statutory benefit

questions.question_text: Stock options for employees are a:
options: Non-financial incentive
Short-term incentive
Statutory benefit
Long-term financial incentive

questions.question_text: Promotion means:
options: Removal from the service of the organisation
Movement to another position at the same level of pay
Movement to a higher position with greater responsibility and pay
Movement to a lower position in the organisation

questions.question_text: Transfer means:
options: A move to a lower position in the hierarchy, with less pay
A termination of the services of the employee by the firm
A move to a higher position in the hierarchy, with more pay
A move to another job at the same level, without any change in pay

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a lateral movement?
options: Promotion from clerk to the senior clerk
Demotion from manager to the assistant
Transfer from sales to marketing at the same level
Dismissal for misconduct

questions.question_text: "Retrenchment" refers to:
options: Termination of services of the employees due to surplus staff
Resignation of the employees on their own wish
Retirement of employees at the age of superannuation
Promotion of employees to a higher level

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a typical cause of employee turnover?
options: Good relations with the superiors
Poor working conditions and low pay
Fair appraisal and clear career paths
Job security and recognition

questions.question_text: The concept of "labour turnover" is computed as the number of separations during a period divided by the:
options: Average number of employees during the period
Total wages paid during the period
Number of new joiners in the period
Number of vacancies in the period

questions.question_text: If 20 employees leave during the year and the average number of employees is 200, the labour turnover is:
HR planning estimates the demand for employees on the basis of:
options: Number of customers who buy from the firm
Past profits and the dividends paid in earlier years
Number of the shareholders registered in the firm
Business plans, technology and expected growth

questions.question_text: In forecasting the supply of employees, HR planners consider:
options: Government taxes and the subsidies for the firm
Retirements, resignations, promotions and transfers
Prices of the raw materials and fuel for the firm
Sales targets and the profit margins of the firm

questions.question_text: The "job analysis" results in:
options: Job description and job specification
Induction and training
Performance appraisal and rewards
Placement and promotion

questions.question_text: A job enrichment programme aims at:
options: Moving the employees from one job to another at regular intervals
Reducing the work load of the employee in the job
Adding the responsibility and decision making to the job to motivate the employee
Increasing the number of the tasks of the same level in the job

questions.question_text: Job enlargement involves:
options: Adding more tasks of the same level to a job
Giving more authority and responsibility in the job
Moving the employee to another department
Reducing the number of tasks in the job

questions.question_text: Job rotation means:
options: Moving employees between jobs to reduce boredom and build skills
Increasing the number of the tasks within the same job
Dismissing the employees after they complete a few years
Adding the higher-level duties to the job of the employee

questions.question_text: A company introduces flexible working hours. This is an example of:
options: Job enrichment
Job evaluation
Job rotation
Alternative work arrangements

questions.question_text: Employee referral as a source of recruitment is:
options: Costly and time-consuming, and open to public scrutiny
Rarely available in practice in any large organisation
Formal and impersonal, since agencies are involved
Quick and cheap, but it may lead to favouritism

questions.question_text: Campus recruitment is useful for hiring:
options: Part-time workers for the odd jobs
Experienced professionals for the senior positions
Retired persons for the advisory posts
Fresh graduates with no experience

questions.question_text: Walk-in interviews are an example of:
options: Internal recruitment
Indirect recruitment
Direct recruitment
Third-party recruitment

questions.question_text: Hiring workers through a placement agency or a consultant is:
options: Internal recruitment
Campus recruitment
Third-party recruitment
Direct recruitment

questions.question_text: Temporary staff hired through a contractor is an example of:
options: Permanent employment on the rolls of the firm
Outsourcing or contract staffing
Internal transfer of the staff within the firm
Job rotation among the employees of the firm

questions.question_text: In a structured interview:
options: The panel decides the questions after the interview ends
Candidates are not asked any questions by the panel
Questions are pre-planned and are the same for every candidate
Questions are asked at random without any prior plan

questions.question_text: In a stress interview, the interviewer:
options: Asks only the simple questions in a friendly manner
Deliberately creates pressure to see how the candidate reacts
Conducts the interview over the telephone
Allows the candidate to ask all the questions

questions.question_text: The "reference check" in the selection process is done to:
options: Orient the candidate to the work
Decide the salary of the candidate
Verify the information given by the candidate
Test the technical skills of the candidate

questions.question_text: A medical examination in selection ensures that the candidate is:
options: Experienced in the job
Qualified for the job
Physically fit for the job
Technically skilled for the job

questions.question_text: The letter that informs the selected candidate of terms of employment is:
options: Application letter
Resignation letter
Appointment letter
Reference letter

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a statutory fringe benefit in India?
options: Company car
Provident fund
Stock option
Performance bonus

questions.question_text: The Employees' State Insurance scheme provides:
options: Retirement pensions for managers of the registered companies
Housing loans for the senior employees of the firm
Education loans for the children of the employees
Medical care and cash benefits during sickness and injury

questions.question_text: Gratuity is paid to an employee:
options: Only if the firm earns a profit in that particular year
On retirement, resignation or death after the minimum service
Every month along with the regular salary of the employee
Only on the festival days of the year, as a gift

questions.question_text: A minimum wage, as per law, is meant to:
options: Ensure a basic standard of living for workers
Limit the maximum salary of the managers
Reduce the labour turnover to nil
Keep the profits of the employers high

questions.question_text: A "fair wage" is one which lies:
options: Below the level of the minimum wage
Without any relation to the minimum wage
Above the level of the maximum wage
Between the minimum wage and the living wage

questions.question_text: Training needs are best identified through:
options: Seniority of employees
Performance appraisal and gap analysis
Salary of employees
Random selection of employees

questions.question_text: The first step in the training process is:
options: Assessment of the training needs
Delivery of the programme
Evaluation of the training programme
Selection of the trainer

questions.question_text: The last step in the training process is:
options: Evaluation of the training programme
Implementation of the programme
Design of the programme
Needs assessment

questions.question_text: Kirkpatrick's levels for the evaluation of training are:
options: Reaction, learning, behaviour and results
Strength, weakness, opportunity and threat
Recruitment, selection, placement and induction
Planning, organising, directing and controlling

questions.question_text: Coaching as a method of development means:
options: Rotation of the jobs among the various departments
On-the-job guidance given by a superior to a subordinate
Classroom lectures that are given by a faculty member
Simulation of the work that is done in a laboratory

questions.question_text: Mentoring involves:
options: Compulsory lectures that are given by the top executives
The use of machines and software to teach the employees
Written tests that are used to evaluate the employees
A senior and experienced person guiding a junior in career growth

questions.question_text: E-learning as a training method has the advantage of:
options: Low cost of preparing the courseware
Flexibility of time and place for the learners
Immediate hands-on practice on the machines
Face-to-face interaction with the trainer

questions.question_text: The process of terminating the services of an employee as a punishment is:
options: Layoff
Transfer
Retrenchment
Dismissal

questions.question_text: In a layoff, the employee is:
options: Transferred to another unit of the organisation
Temporarily without work due to a lack of demand but not terminated
Permanently removed from the services of the organisation
Promoted to a higher position in the organisation

questions.question_text: A voluntary retirement scheme is aimed at:
options: Training the employees in the new skills needed by the firm
Increasing the workforce through the hiring of new staff
Promoting the senior employees to the higher posts in the firm
Reducing the workforce by offering attractive terms to those opting out

questions.question_text: "Right person for the right job" refers to:
options: Placement
Training
Recruitment
Appraisal

questions.question_text: The advantage of staffing is that it:
options: Ensures competent persons for the various jobs
Maintains the stock of materials of the firm
Prepares the financial statements of the firm
Fixes the prices of the products of the firm

questions.question_text: An HR manager finds that the firm will need 50 more engineers next year. This is the result of:
options: Performance appraisal
Human resource planning
Induction
Job evaluation

questions.question_text: A firm has 500 employees and plans to increase output by 20%. If employee productivity is unchanged, the additional employees needed are:
If the firm in the previous question improves productivity by 10%, the employees needed for 20% more output (approximately) are:
options: About 545
About 600
About 450
About 500

questions.question_text: A firm has 40 vacancies and gets 400 applications. Of these 100 pass the test and 20 qualify at the interview. The selection ratio is:
"Equal pay for equal work" is a principle enshrined in:
options: The Constitution of India as a directive principle
The Companies Act as a requirement for the dividends
The Income Tax Act as a deduction
The Sale of Goods Act as a clause

questions.question_text: Under the Equal Remuneration principle, a male and a female worker doing the same job must be:
options: Paid based on the age
Paid based on the marital status
Paid based on gender
Paid the same remuneration

questions.question_text: Talent management involves:
options: Preparing the annual budget of the firm for the next year
Selecting the machines for use in the factory of the firm
Attracting, developing and retaining high-performing employees
Auditing the accounts of the firm at the end of the year

questions.question_text: Succession planning is the process of:
options: Preparing employees to fill key positions when they fall vacant
Distributing the profits of the company to its shareholders
Recording the minutes of the meetings of the board of directors
Selecting new shareholders for the company at a general meeting

questions.question_text: The "grievance redressal" system in an organisation aims to:
options: Punish the employees who complain
Ignore the complaints of the employees
Resolve the complaints of the employees fairly and quickly
Increase the number of complaints from the employees

questions.question_text: An exit interview is held with employees who:
options: Are leaving the organisation, to learn their reasons for leaving
Are undergoing a training programme, to know its usefulness
Have just joined the organisation, to know their first impressions
Are about to be promoted, to know their future plans

questions.question_text: Employee engagement refers to:
options: The number of hours that the employees work in a week
The emotional commitment of employees to the organisation
The amount of salary that the employees get in a month
The average age of the employees working in the firm

questions.question_text: The Indian law on sexual harassment at the workplace requires every organisation to have:
options: A board committee on audit
A works council
An Internal Complaints Committee
A trade union

questions.question_text: Diversity management at the workplace aims at:
options: Fixing an identical salary for all the employees of the firm
Hiring employees from only one background to avoid conflict
Removing employees of different backgrounds from the firm
Valuing differences among employees in gender, age and background

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a non-financial incentive?
options: Profit sharing among all the employees of the firm
A year-end bonus linked to the profits of the firm
Recognition and an opportunity for growth in the firm
Stock options granted to the senior employees of the firm

questions.question_text: Payment of wages on the basis of the number of units produced is:
options: Time rate system
Differential rate system
Profit sharing
Piece rate system

questions.question_text: Payment of wages on the basis of the time worked is:
options: Piece rate system
Time rate system
Incentive system
Bonus system

questions.question_text: If a worker produces 40 units at a piece rate of Rs 15 per unit, the earning is:
options: Rs 375
Rs 150
Rs 55
Rs 600

questions.question_text: A worker is paid Rs 120 per hour for 8 hours and Rs 150 per hour for overtime of 2 hours. Total pay is:
A good training programme has:
options: Clear objectives linked to the performance gaps of the employees
A fixed schedule irrespective of the needs of the employees
No evaluation of its results after the programme ends
Trainees who are selected at random from the staff

questions.question_text: The HRM function is described as:
options: Needed only in the large firms
Concerned only with salaries
A one-time activity at the start
Pervasive, continuous and people-oriented
